title.title: Brennan's conjecture, and Kraetzer's formula fails
title.subtitle: Claim: $\int |\varphi'|^s\,dA < \infty$ for every $4/3 < s < 4$, for every conformal map onto the disk

plain: Squash a wild shape onto a disk without tearing: how violently can the squashing pile up near the edge?

beats.text: How badly can a conformal map compress area near a wild boundary?
The upper end stuck at about 3.42 for a quarter-century. The claim reaches 4
A companion: Kraetzer's 1996 formula fails at $t = -1$, by an uncomputed gap

steps: Suppose some map compresses area faster than the conjecture allows
Turn that growth rate into a random law over normalized maps
Its saddle points and peaks cannot pair up: contradiction

data.assume: a map that grows too fast
data.impossible: saddles and peaks cannot pair up

sources.quote: Brennan (1978) conjectured the range 4/3<s<4; the lower end and s<3 were classical
Bertilsson's 1999 thesis pushed the upper end to about 3.42, and it stuck there for a quarter-century.
Kraetzer conjectured in 1996, from numerics on Julia sets, that the bounded-class spectrum is exactly $t^2/4$ for $|t| \le 2$.
The paper proves $B_b(-1) < 1/4$, so Kraetzer's formula fails at $t = -1$. It does not say by how much: the gap $\epsilon$ is never computed.
The B_S(t)=|t|-1 for all t≤-2 statement is in the paper but not in the comparator file.
